detail: hybrid_dispatch.parse_strace_reads resolves every non-absolute openat path against the checkout root. Directory-fd-relative opens -- openat(3, "coordinator", O_RDONLY|O_NONBLOCK|O_CLOEXEC) -- are emitted by shutil.rmtree's fd walk during tempfile.TemporaryDirectory cleanup, which every Python unit-test oracle in this repo uses. Validating V5-M1-driver-stop-conditions on devbox reported the oracle as reading 'coordinator', 'repo-x', 'wt': three paths that do not exist in the repository. Reproduced directly with strace -f -qq -e trace=openat,open,stat,readlink at 31f6fa562c85; 38 such lines, all fd-relative, and they were the ONLY offenders -- every real read was inside readable_context_paths union writable_patch_paths. Fix: trust a relative openat path only when the first argument is AT_FDCWD. That is templates/dispatch/scripts/hybrid_dispatch.py, a manifest-protected path, so handover section 7 says stop and report rather than edit it. M-1 was frozen instead via the section-1 sanctioned off-devbox route (--allow-untraced-oracle, read_trace recorded as skipped:untraced) with the devbox trace evidence attached to PR #56.

detail: Handover rule 2 makes oracle.reference_patch mandatory on mechanical_bulk packets but does not say where it may live. detail: The L-1 driver runs gh pr create with cwd set to the packet's disposable worktree so gh resolves the repository from there rather than from the coordinator checkout. That worktree is a clone with no remotes, so gh exits 1 with 'no git remotes found'. Both V5-M1 dispatches reached disposition candidate with every gate green and every stage exiting 0, and both then failed at the PR step for this reason. Until L-1 landed no run had ever reached a candidate disposition, so the PR step had never executed. dispatch_release.py is not a protected path, so this is loop-fixable; it is a candidate packet for the M-series remainder. Both M-1 PRs were opened by hand from the gate receipt's own diff.

detail: Packet V5-M2-driver-retry-policy (handover M-2, spec row L-4) at 458f4b43bc47, route mechanical_bulk, opencode-go/deepseek-v4-flash, worker agentworker on devbox. Both attempts produced NO edits: gate diff-nonempty false, touched_paths empty, agentops.dispatch.tests.driver exit 1. Two different failure modes, neither informational. Attempt 1 ($0.093734, 198304 tokens): the final assistant step finished with reason=length at 131072 output tokens -- the worker tried to emit the whole restructured file in one response and was truncated before any write landed. Attempt 2 ($0.008456, 100258 tokens): stopped on tool-calls after listing docs/evidence/packets/, having spent its turn looking for other packets rather than implementing. Containment held on both; both runs were qualification-eligible. M-1's gate-red-twice stop then fired exactly as encoded -- ledger 458f4b43bc47 -> 2, report stop condition gate-red-twice, exit 1, no PR -- which is the first production exercise of the L-2 stop conditions and it worked. Handover section 7 says stop the sequence and do not reshape the packet beyond one retry, so the packet is left exactly as frozen. Evidence: attempt-1 report, attempt-2 report and attempt-2 receipt preserved under docs/evidence/reviews/. opencode export failed on both sessions (truncated JSON), so the raw worker transcript survives only inside the run receipt's worker.stdout. Diagnosis for the owner: this packet is one outcome but its EDIT SHAPE -- restructure a 400-line function -- exceeds what this tier can emit in one response. Rule 1 bounds a packet by outcome, file and oracle; it does not bound the size of the rewrite, and that is the gap.

detail: V5-M6a is the first dispatch to run on the M-8 driver. remote-add and push both succeeded -- M-8's fix works, and the branch hybrid/v5-m6a-cost-hook-artifacts-root reached origin from the loop itself. Two gaps remain, both additive and both in templates/dispatch/scripts/dispatch_release.py, neither in the current brief and neither actioned. (1) gh pr create failed with 'GraphQL: Body is too long (maximum is 65536 characters)'. The receipt is the PR body per section 4.5, and V5-M6a's receipt is 165515 bytes because it carries the worker's full stdout -- which is now the only transcript, since the hand-pass removed the opencode export path. Section 4.5 cannot hold as written: the body has to be a bounded summary that points at the receipt beside it. (2) More seriously, the pushed branch points at cc3e9c37adbd, the packet's starting_commit. The driver never commits the worker's changes: post_gates reads the diff from the working tree with git diff --name-only <starting_commit>, and nothing between the worker finishing and the push ever commits it. Even with a short enough body the PR would have been empty. Order matters for whoever fixes this: commit in the worktree, then push, then create. Both are additive, unprotected, rule-9-shaped packets.

detail: Sibling of hand-pass item A, found while freezing V5-M9. parse_strace_reads resolves every AT_FDCWD-relative openat path against the checkout root, which is only correct while the traced process's cwd IS the checkout. An oracle that runs a real subprocess elsewhere -- V5-M9's RealGitCommitTests runs a real git with cwd set to a temp repo -- makes git emit openat(AT_FDCWD, "refs/heads/main", ...) and the parser reports phantom reads of <checkout>/refs/heads/main, <checkout>/objects/pack, <checkout>/tracked.txt and so on. Item A fixed the directory-fd case; this is the cwd case and the same function owns both. templates/dispatch/scripts/hybrid_dispatch.py is protected, so it was not touched: instead the two real-git fixtures moved to templates/dispatch/tests/test_realgit_dispatch_commit.py, deliberately named so it falls outside the packet's traced glob test_dispatch_release*.py while plain discover still runs it for the section 4.6 gate. The proof is kept, the trace stays mandatory, and no declared path was widened. General shape of the limitation for whoever fixes it: a relative path is only meaningful against a cwd the tracer knows, so either resolve nothing relative, or trace chdir/execve to track cwd per pid.

detail: Found when L-4's retry fired in production for the first time, on V5-M9. hybrid_dispatch resolves its policy from AGENTOPS_ROOT, which defaults to /projects/dev/agentops. dispatch_release.hybrid_cmd passes --repo-root and --packet but never --agentops-root, so every stage the driver runs reads the policy from that default path -- on devbox a stale clone at 384f8bc -- while the coordinator's own validate was invoked with --agentops-root . against the packet's checkout. The two disagreed the moment the hand-pass raised mechanical_bulk max_attempts from 1 to 2: validate accepted the retry packet, and the driver's run stage refused it with 'attempt 2 exceeds max_attempts 1 for route mechanical_bulk'. The retry L-4 grants was consumed by a harness mismatch rather than by the worker. Everything else the two policies say happened to agree, which is why this went unnoticed through five green packets -- the route model, the ceilings and the gate set hash all matched by luck, not by construction. Worked around for now by exporting AGENTOPS_ROOT=/tmp/v5-coordinator in the devbox coordinator env; the real fix is for the driver to pass --agentops-root explicitly so a packet is judged and run against one policy. That is dispatch_release.py, unprotected and additive -- a packet, not a hand-pass. The false red it produced was removed from the attempt ledger for this starting_commit, because L-4's one retry had not actually been spent on the work.

detail: Corrects ad:01M0R1MY48830T0XZ41B9G8CY3. devbox exports AGENTOPS_HYBRID_POLICY=/etc/agentops/hybrid-dispatch.json and AGENTOPS_HYBRID_WORKER_CONFIG=/etc/agentops/opencode.hybrid.json, and load_policy honours that override ahead of agentops_root -- deliberately, per its own docstring: 'a deployed host may pin an immutable copy so the host never silently follows a mutable source checkout'. That is the pin working as designed. The hand-pass raised mechanical_bulk max_attempts to 2 in the source checkout, but the deployed copy at /etc/agentops/ still says 1, so L-4's first production retry was refused by the host's own policy rather than by any harness bug. Pinning AGENTOPS_ROOT changed nothing, because the override wins. The real gap is a deployment one: a route-policy change in the repository does not reach devbox until /etc/agentops/hybrid-dispatch.json is updated through the infra path (gitops-nixos hosts/devbox), and there is no sudo on that host. Not overridden here: unsetting AGENTOPS_HYBRID_POLICY would defeat exactly the property the pin exists for. The separate observation that dispatch_release.hybrid_cmd never passes --agentops-root remains true and still worth fixing, but it was not the cause.

detail: Both V5-M9 attempts produced no diff. The transcript shows why: nine tool calls, every one a read, across the driver, all six sibling driver oracles and the manifest -- then the run ended with nothing written, at 76798 and 68000 tokens for $0.0098 and $0.0090. The packet declared seven readable_context_paths because its starts_red command was agentops.dispatch.tests.driver, whose glob reads every test_dispatch_release*.py, and the read trace requires each of them declared. So a rule-1-shaped change -- one outcome, one writable file, additive -- was handed a reading list four files longer than it needed. This is the coordinator's defect and it is a new failure mode, distinct from V5-M2's: not the edit shape but the context breadth. The fix is a narrowing rather than a widening: register agentops.dispatch.tests.commit running only the packet's own oracle, and declare only the driver and that oracle as readable. Recorded before re-freezing so the two reds are attributed to the packet, not to the tier.

detail: Three dispatches of V5-M9, all no-diff, and the third transcript names the cause -- none of it the model. The worker made nine tool calls: four reads, one bash that the worker profile REFUSED ('The user has specified a rule which prevents you from using this specific tool call'), three greps and one grep that ERRORED with 'Ripgrep JSON record exceeded 65536 bytes'. Then hybrid_dispatch's own context-churn guard stopped the run: churn_stop = {reason: churn_no_mutation, detail: '9 tool steps without a completed mutation (limit 8)'}. So the packet's max_reasoning_steps_without_mutation of 8 -- carried unchanged from V5-P1a through every packet this session -- is spent by failing exploration before a write is ever attempted. Two contributing causes worth separating. (1) grep dies on this repository because docs/evidence/reviews/ now holds 165KB-230KB single-line JSON driver reports that I committed in #58 and #66; ripgrep's JSON record limit is 65536 bytes. The worker's workspace is a full clone, so every worker now trips this. (2) bash is denied to the worker by profile, which is correct containment, but it means a denied bash still costs a churn step. This matters directly for M-10: that row proposes committing receipts (165KB) under docs/evidence/receipts/<task>/ on the packet branch, which would put MORE oversized JSON into every future worker's clone and make this worse on every subsequent packet. Recommend deciding that before M-10 is built. Separately, L-4's retry cannot run on devbox at all: the host pins an immutable policy at /etc/agentops/hybrid-dispatch.json (AGENTOPS_HYBRID_POLICY) which still says max_attempts 1, and there is no sudo on that host, so every retry is refused with 'attempt 2 exceeds max_attempts 1'. Stopping under section 7 rather than reshaping the packet a third time; it has already been re-frozen twice, both times on freeze-time feedback (the read trace, then the reading list).

detail: V5-M10-bounded-pr-body, attempt 1: no diff, no churn stop, $0.104515 and 408693 tokens -- the highest spend of any packet this session. The transcript shows sensible work (four reads, one well-aimed grep) and then a final step that finished with reason=length at 131072 output tokens, having emitted no tool call. That is the identical signature to V5-M2 attempt 1, and it is rule 9's boundary rather than a new failure mode: the packet is additive and touches one file, but it adds FOUR things at once -- a secret-scan function, a receipt-capture step, a PR-body generator, and a PR_STEP_NAMES change with the sub-step renaming that follows from it. Rule 9 bounds a packet by additive-versus-restructuring; V5-M2 and now V5-M10 say it also needs bounding by how much is added. The oracle already partitions cleanly along the seam, into four test classes, so the split is available without rewriting it: SecretScanTests (3 fixtures, a pure function, no control flow), BodyTests (4 fixtures, the generator plus pointing --body-file at it), CaptureTests plus SubStepNameTests (17 fixtures, the capture step and the naming). Recommend M-10a/M-10b/M-10c on that seam, in that order, since the capture step is the only one that depends on the other two. The one retry section 7 grants was not spent: it is unavailable on devbox until gitops-nixos #17 is deployed, because the host's immutable policy at /etc/agentops/hybrid-dispatch.json still caps mechanical_bulk at max_attempts 1. Stopping rather than reshaping the packet unasked.
